answer: Sybil resistance can come from latency forensics rather than stake: each epoch the registry records nanosecond arrival timestamps of every agent's submission and clusters them by inter-arrival rhythm. Independent agents emit a jittery pulse driven by their own clocks and retry logic, while a farm of sock-puppets shares one scheduler, leaking a common cadence. Clustering residual timing fingerprints against the epoch's zenith (peak hour) exposes whole batches; suspect accounts must re-anchor with a fresh independent proof-of-execution before they earn, so cheap clones never accrue weight.
